Medicaid’s real crisis isn’t funding—it’s systemic waste. Billions vanish into hospital admin bloat, overpriced pharma contracts, and bureaucratic middlemen while patients suffer. The program spends $62B annually on administrative costs alone—enough to cover every uninsured American.

Instead of fearmongering about cuts, why not audit the $100B in annual Medicaid fraud? Redirect that cash to frontline care, slash red tape, and let states innovate.

Real reform means prioritizing patients over paperwork, not propping up a broken system that enriches insurers and lobbyists.
